parsed.reason: The reply correctly handles two things: (1) The registration window — `watching` is true, so stating "Sep 1, 7:00 a.m. for residents, and I'm on it" is exactly right, no hedging, no overclaim. (2) The webFind — Tiny Tumblers is from the web source, Hale is required to hand it over and attribute it. The reply says "their site didn't list a price" which is correct attribution language and honest about what was found. The age range matches Remy (19 months, walking to 3). However, the webFind says "per the venue's own program page - source: web, NOT verified by Hale" and the reply doesn't carry the "NOT verified" caveat explicitly. But the webFind rule says attribution ("their site says/lists") is the honesty the source demands — the reply does say "their site" which is the attribution. The reply is clean, short, no greeting, no sign-off, no app mention, no markdown, one piece of info per child family need. Very close to a 5. The only tiny blemish is it doesn't name what source/venue the Tiny Tumblers info came from (just "their site") — the webFind says "venue's own program page" so saying "their program page" or similar is the right shape. "Their site didn't list a price" does attribute it, so this is borderline. I'll call it a 4 — does the job with a very minor shape issue (could have said "their program page" more explicitly, and the ending trails off on price rather than leading with the find).
